# Pre-registration: HAT-P-32 b, MicroObservatory night of 2026-10-06 UT

Scaffold from tools/mobs_night.py, judgment lines edited 2026-10-06 before any fit (commit time in git).
The first CLEAN, moonless, full HAT-P-32 b night since row 57: no MOONLIT flag, clear 104/104, comparisons chosen by the
10-05 rule (none at or above 80% of saturation on the clearest frame; peaks 1895-3157 ADU, the top one close to the line).

Frames: 104, 05:03 to 10:13 UT, 60.0 s Clear.
Archive (NEA pscomppars, fetched 2026-10-06 18:12 UTC): P 2.15000820 +/- 1.3e-07 d,
T0 2455867.402743 +/- 4.9e-05, T14 3.120 h, Rp/Rs 0.1489 (depth 2.22%), a/Rs 5.344,
inc 88.98, e 0.159, Teff 6001.0, V 11.439. Epoch 2536: predicted Tmid 2461319.82354 (07:45 UT),
ingress 06:12, egress 09:19; 69 min pre-ingress and 54 min post-egress in the window
(full). Propagated ephemeris bar 0.5 min.

Predictions:
- Sky judged by stars per frame and the target's aperture flux (night_triage), not the background.
  If the counts hold through 06:12-09:19 and the seed target is >200 ADU above background:
  QC PASS (a V 11.4 target at 953 ADU peak, clear all night: the strongest MObs case in the ledger).
- Scatter, from the V-magnitude calibration (0.84% at V 11.57 on 2026-09-05, +0.05%/mag from three clean nights, revised 2026-09-18):
  ~0.83%. On a 2.22% depth that is scatter/depth 0.38; with 0.425 giving
  8.2 min at ~3 min cadence, expected Tmid bar ~5 min (x0.63 bias correction from 17 fitted rows; honest range 3-8, the model predicts bars only to a factor ~1.8).
  Under 2 min: calibration wrong the other way. Over 13.7 min: worse night than the counts show (3x is ~2 sigma of the spread).
- CLOCK: ExoClock (publish.ts, verified 09-22) epoch 2093 Tmid 2461319.82314 BJD_TDB, bar 0.15 min (archive is 0.6 min later).
  Expected O-C = the calibration offset, +1.9 +/- 1.0 min. Combined bar C = sqrt(fit_bar^2 + 1.0^2).
  Outcomes, in order, each result in exactly one:
  1. Transit QC FAIL -> no timing; recorded as such.
  2. post_run_check prints any WARN for the transit-fit comparison -> ONE pre-stated refit with that comparison removed
     from the list (one variable); the refit is then the measurement for 3-5. If the refit also WARNs -> inconclusive.
  3. |O-C - 1.9| > 3 C -> surprise: an injection test on three on-chip stars BEFORE any timing is quoted.
  4. |O-C - 1.9| <= 2 C -> consistent with the calibration: the night becomes a timing point (moonless, clean
     comparisons) and joins the calibration, which is recomputed and restated.
  5. Otherwise -> quoted with its O-C, not added to the calibration.
  A different reducer's result on the same night (shared privately) is NOT used here.
- Depth within 1 sigma of 2.22%; Rp/Rs within 1 sigma of 0.1489.
- If stars-per-frame falls by more than half at any point between 06:12 and 09:19, or the target is under
  ~200 ADU above background in the seed frame: expect FAIL or a rejected night, and the record will say so
  with no depth or timing claim.
- Any printed bar under 0.001 d is a replaced bar (#1401) and gets refit before the ledger.
- First-frame coordinates from a local plate solve; drift by star-pair voting; comps in the triage box within a
  brightness factor of the target; #1409 confirms the rest.
- Not submitted regardless; checkpoint holds.

parameters.Fit parameter point estimate: Best-fit likelihood point; uncertainties are posterior spread.
parameters.Pre-UltraNest LM boundary scout note: LM solution and covariance envelope were interior after 3 iteration(s).
parameters.Out-of-transit baseline parameter-fit no: Used a0 and a2 from the previous fast UltraNest fit for the full-resolution final run.
parameters.Out-of-transit baseline detrending note: only 19 pre-ingress and 11 post-egress out-of-transit point(s) were available; need more than 12 on each side to fit a linear baseline.
parameters.Final residual rejection note: No residual outliers exceeded 3.0 sigma from the iterated median residual (0.0413%, stdev=0.6629%).
parameters.Uncertainty interpretation note: The primary Rp/R* and radius-ratio area-depth uncertainties use model+red-noise when available. The red-noise uncertainty inflates the data-fit standard error by a residual time-binning beta factor before combining it with the model posterior. The flux baseline red-noise uncertainty is the out-of-transit baseline component used for the final-plot baseline band; the transit-depth red-noise uncertainty already includes both the in-transit and baseline terms. The same residual time-binning beta factor is applied to the posterior uncertainties for Tmid, a/Rs, inclination, and impact parameter when reporting their primary model+red-noise uncertainties. The flux-scatter equivalent is also shown as a diagnostic of the full residual scatter around the model.
